title: Reattach your detached wrist camera
instruction: Reattach the loose camera to its mount on your left wrist. Release it once it is secured.
setup: Fixed bimanual YAM station: rigid metal arms with parallel grippers, bases (0,+0.305,0.750) and (0,-0.305,0.750) m, initial joints [0,1,1,-0.6,0,0] rad and open grippers. Wooden tabletop 1.10x1.30x0.06 m, centre (0.36,0,0.7175) m, top z=0.7475 m. Rigid polymer camera housing 40x36x28 mm,55 g, spawned at (0.36,-0.19,0.7725) m with identity body rotation and allowed to settle; front lens on +Y. Rear polymer shoe nominally20x4x24 mm; aluminium channel with20.4 mm internal width, retaining lips, stop, two7 mm-square supports, and a spring-loaded retaining tooth with an external pull tab and a tapered shoe nose. Exact part dimensions in mechanism_dimensions.json; original optical target in native_camera_target.json. Apple66 mm/120 g at XY(0.30,0.28), orange64 mm/110 g at XY(0.40,0.26); natural fruit mesh appearance, rigid contact, mesh bottoms placed on table. Station floor, lighting and metal top-camera stand:110x110x16 mm foot,12 mm radius mast,9 mm radius arm,50x42x22 mm camera housing; calibrated transforms and lengths in the pinned environment. Top and right wrist feeds remain available; left feed follows detached housing. Fruit is context only. All materials describe physical counterparts; no elastic fruit/cable simulation.
scoring: 0.25: entire camera envelope >20 mm above table for1 s, closing gripper command and TCP within50 mm of envelope; pickup credit persists unless invalidated. 0.5: optical position error <=5 mm and rotation error <=5 degrees for1 s while held or latched. 0.75: verified entry through channel, seating and current latch engagement with alignment maintained. 1.0: aligned latched camera and advancing camera frame delivery persist2 s after other TCP is >80 mm from envelope. Alignment/release intervals reset when interrupted. Below-table drop (body z < tabletop-50 mm) invalidates all credit. No READY-return condition.
fidelity: Housing, tapered shoe, guide, stop, tooth and external release tab use rigid collision geometry. Contact retracts a spring-loaded prismatic tooth during insertion; it returns into the shoe notch. Pulling the external tab retracts this same tooth for removal. No fixed joint connects camera and wrist. The live camera follows the housing throughout. Cable forces and electrical reconnection are outside the task.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; demo: 1.0. Model: 1800 control steps in one continuous session.
context: Automating installation and restoration of a robot’s own sensing hardware can reduce manual intervention in robot setup and maintenance. This task requires inserting and retaining a live camera on the robot’s moving wrist, with the receiving arm positioning its mount for the other arm; the camera must remain secured after release.
reset_notes: A fresh process restores the fixed scene, robot initial joints, detached camera and spring plunger. For mechanical removal, support the camera, pull the external tab outward to retract the tooth, then slide the camera out of the guide.
